BoardSettings.description: How the boards look (looks.py): the pieces and the squares' colours.

pieces.description: The pieces on every board: Sidecoach's own, a freely licensed set, or your own images.
pieces.label: Pieces
pieces.title: Pieces

theme.description: The colours of the board's squares.
theme.label: Board colours
theme.title: Theme

BoardSettings.title: BoardSettings

fps.description: How often the screen is read. Ten is plenty for a game; more costs CPU.
fps.label: Frames per second
fps.title: Fps

stuck_seconds.description: How long you may think on a move before the coach offers a nudge. With a clock it comes sooner when you are short of time.
stuck_seconds.label: Nudge after (seconds)
stuck_seconds.title: Stuck Seconds

quiet.description: No verdicts, questions or nudges on its own; the coach answers when you ask.
quiet.label: Only speak when asked
quiet.title: Quiet

persona.description: The coach's manner: how it phrases things. The lessons and the rules are the same in every one.
persona.label: Manner
persona.title: Persona

verify.description: A second model reads every reply the coach drafts and only the ones that stick to the facts are spoken. Empty is off; 'same' uses the coach's own model; a provider name uses that one (slower, safer).
verify.label: Verifier
verify.title: Verify

verify_model.description: The model the second opinion uses, when a provider is named above.
verify_model.label: Verifier's model
verify_model.title: Verify Model

summarise_every.description: Every this many half-moves, what was said earlier is folded into a short summary, so the model reads less as the game goes on. 0 keeps everything.
summarise_every.label: Summarise every (plies)
summarise_every.title: Summarise Every

compact_record.description: Sound moves nobody spoke about are shown to the model as a plain list instead of one line each, to keep what it reads short.
compact_record.label: Compact move record
compact_record.title: Compact Record

verbalized_sampling.description: The model drafts a few phrasings and one is spoken, so the coach does not say the same thing the same way twice. Off is a little quicker.
verbalized_sampling.label: Varied phrasing
verbalized_sampling.title: Verbalized Sampling

local_verdicts.description: A best, excellent or book move gets its short word written from the board itself: instant and free. Only good, great and brilliant moves go to the model. Off sends every move to the model, which is slower and costs more.
local_verdicts.label: Quick verdicts from the board
local_verdicts.title: Local Verdicts

inaccuracy.description: A move that costs at least this much of your winning chances is called an inaccuracy (0.04 is 4%).
inaccuracy.label: Inaccuracy threshold
inaccuracy.title: Inaccuracy

mistake.description: A move that costs at least this much of your winning chances is called a mistake, and the coach explains it.
mistake.label: Mistake threshold
mistake.title: Mistake

blunder.description: A move that costs at least this much of your winning chances is called a blunder.
blunder.label: Blunder threshold
blunder.title: Blunder

decisive_gap.description: When the best move is better than the next by this much, the moment is decisive and the coach asks you to slow down before you move.
decisive_gap.label: Decisive-moment gap
decisive_gap.title: Decisive Gap

only_move_gap.description: When every other move loses at least this much, the best move is the only move.
only_move_gap.label: Only-move gap
only_move_gap.title: Only Move Gap

excellent.description: A move that costs less than this is called excellent, as good as the best.
excellent.label: Excellent threshold
excellent.title: Excellent

decided.description: Beyond this winning chance (0.9 is 90%) the game is decided, and small losses no longer earn a lesson.
decided.label: Game decided beyond
decided.title: Decided

multipv.description: How many of the best moves Stockfish reports for each position, and so how many the coach can compare. More costs time.
multipv.label: Candidate lines
multipv.title: Multipv

threads.description: Processor threads Stockfish may use. More is faster to a point, and warms the phone; leave some for the game.
threads.label: CPU threads
threads.title: Threads

hash_mb.description: Memory Stockfish keeps for positions it has already seen, in MB. More helps a deep search; 64 is plenty on a phone.
hash_mb.label: Memory (MB)
hash_mb.title: Hash Mb

depth.description: How deep Stockfish looks at every position. Deeper is more accurate and slower; 14 is what a phone reaches in a few seconds, and stronger than any player.
depth.label: Depth
depth.title: Depth

pv_plies.description: How far ahead each line is shown, in half-moves, when the coach gives a line.
pv_plies.label: Line length (plies)
pv_plies.title: Pv Plies

score_model.description: How Stockfish's evaluation becomes your winning chance. 'As people play' is fitted to games between people, so a pawn up means what it means for you; Stockfish's own numbers assume perfect play, where a knight up is already won.
score_model.label: Scoring
score_model.title: Score Model

max_seconds.description: The most time one position may take. A think that runs long is cut off here so the coach keeps up with the game.
max_seconds.label: Time limit per position (s)
max_seconds.title: Max Seconds

choice_labels.auto: Automatic — use it when it works (recommended)

mode.description: Whether the voice, speech recognition and the board reader run on the NVIDIA graphics card (CUDA). Automatic fetches what that needs once and falls back to the CPU on any trouble.
mode.label: Hardware acceleration
mode.title: Mode

choice_labels.local: A model on your own computer (LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM)

provider.description: The AI model the coach thinks with. OpenAI is the one the coach was tested on; a model on your own computer costs nothing per game; with no model the coach still speaks, from the board and its templates.
provider.label: Provider
provider.title: Provider

model.description: The model's name. Empty uses the provider's default (gpt-5.6-luna; qwen3.8-max; for a local server, whichever model it has loaded).
model.label: Model
model.title: Model

models.description: The model chosen for each service, by service: switching to another service and back brings that service's model back.
models.label: Models
models.title: Models

base_url.description: Where the model is served. For a model on your computer, that computer's address on your network and LM Studio's port, such as http://192.168.1.20:1234/v1. Empty means http://localhost:1234/v1, which on a phone is the phone itself.
base_url.label: Server address
base_url.title: Base Url

reasoning_effort.description: How long the model may think before it answers. More is slower and costs more; medium is what the coach was evaluated at.
reasoning_effort.label: Thinking effort
reasoning_effort.title: Reasoning Effort

routine_effort.description: A word on a fine move needs no deep thought: with none it is spoken in under a second, at the least cost. Lessons and answers keep the effort above.
routine_effort.label: Thinking effort for quick remarks
routine_effort.title: Routine Effort

price_prompt_per_m.description: What the provider charges per million tokens sent to it, from its price list. Only used for the running cost shown in the status strip; the app charges nothing.
price_prompt_per_m.label: Price per million prompt tokens (USD)
price_prompt_per_m.title: Price Prompt Per M

price_cached_per_m.description: The provider's price per million tokens it had already seen (cached), usually much lower. For the cost shown in the status strip.
price_cached_per_m.label: Price per million cached prompt tokens (USD)
price_cached_per_m.title: Price Cached Per M

price_completion_per_m.description: The provider's price per million tokens it writes back, thinking included. For the cost shown in the status strip.
price_completion_per_m.label: Price per million answer tokens (USD)
price_completion_per_m.title: Price Completion Per M

timeout_s.description: How long the coach waits for the model each time it asks. Past this it gives up on that reply and speaks from the board instead, so a slow service never stalls the game.
timeout_s.label: Timeout (seconds)
timeout_s.title: Timeout S

rating_low.description: The bottom of your rating where you play (chess.com, Lichess, over the board); a rough band is fine. The coach pitches what it says at it.
rating_low.label: Your rating, from
rating_low.title: Rating Low

chesscom_user.description: Your username on chess.com. Game Review brings in your recent games with it and knows which side you played. Only your public games are read, through chess.com's public data; nothing is sent to your account.
chesscom_user.label: Your chess.com username
chesscom_user.title: Chesscom User

lichess_user.description: Your username on Lichess, for the same: your recent public games, and which side was yours.
lichess_user.label: Your Lichess username
lichess_user.title: Lichess User

voice.description: The coach's voice: Kokoro's English ones, American or British, female or male.
voice.label: Voice
voice.title: Voice

muted.description: The coach stays silent; its words still show, on the panel and in the captions. The speaker button at the top of the panel does the same.
muted.label: Mute the coach's voice
muted.title: Muted

lang.description: The voice's accent code: en-us for the American voices, en-gb for the British.
lang.label: Language code
lang.title: Lang

choice_labels.ptt: While I hold the talk button

listen.description: How the coach hears you. To talk while you hold, press and hold the round button beside the question box.
listen.label: Listening
listen.title: Listen

captions.description: Shows what the coach says in a small box over other apps, like Live Caption, so you can read it while you play. Touch and hold the box to move it; double-tap it to see more; tap it for its buttons; drag it onto the cross at the bottom of the screen to turn captions off. CC at the top of the panel turns them on and off too. The first time, Android asks you to let Sidecoach display over other apps.
captions.label: Captions over other apps
captions.title: Captions

captions_keep.description: Keeps the caption box on screen all the time, over every app, Sidecoach too: its buttons, and the coach's last words once it has spoken. Off, the box comes up when the coach speaks, fades a few seconds after, and steps aside while Sidecoach itself is open. The pin beside CC at the top of the panel does the same.
captions_keep.label: Keep captions on screen
captions_keep.title: Captions Keep

captions_text_color.description: The colour of the captions' words.
captions_text_color.label: Text colour
captions_text_color.title: Captions Text Color

captions_background.description: The colour of the box behind the words.
captions_background.label: Background colour
captions_background.title: Captions Background

captions_opacity.description: How solid the box is, in percent: 100 hides what is behind it, lower lets it show through.
captions_opacity.label: Background opacity (%)
captions_opacity.title: Captions Opacity

captions_text_size.description: How big the captions' words are; 17 is the usual size.
captions_text_size.label: Text size
captions_text_size.title: Captions Text Size
